newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas prices retreat amid lighter demand.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas prices retreat amid lighter demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices drifted lower Tuesday amid a weaker futures market and a drop in trading volume due to a gas conference in Houston, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf prices fell 10 cents to the mid-$1.80s to low-$1.90s per mmBtu, with Henry Hub mostly in the low-$1.90s.
In south Texas, prices were similarly lower in the mid-$1.80s as temperatures in the state hovered a few degrees above normal.
NYMEX Henry Hub April natgas was down 1.9 cents at $1.89 per mmBtu at 1307 EST.
In the East, New York city-gate prices remained in the mid-$2.30s to about $2.40, supported by continued cold in the region.
However, in the Appalachian region, prices were down an average of five cents to about $2.09-2.10. Late morning deals were reported done on Columbia Gas as low as $2.
In the Midcontinent, prices tumbled into the mid-$1.70s to low-$1.80s, down more than 10 cents from Monday. Most Panhandle prices carried about a five-cent premium to prices on ANR, SW.
Chicago city-gate values lost about five to seven cents to about $2.05, while prices at the Detroit city-gate drifted down to about $2.15-2.18.

Detroit Edison said earlier today it expected to restore service by late tonight to the remaining 5,000 customers still without power. The utility, which serves more than two million customers, estimated that about 422,000 customers were initially affected by last Thursday's ice storm-related outages.
Further west where temperatures have been hovering above normal, Permian basin prices slipped nine cents to the mid-$1.70s early and the low-$1.70s shortly before nomination deadlines.
At the southern California border, limited volumes of gas traded in the high-$1.70s to about $1.80.
The 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California was still in "hot standby" this morning and expected to be back on line today, the NRC reported.
